back: The mean of (actual − forecast). It shows the direction: positive means the forecast is too low.
Sum of absolute errors divided by sum of actuals. A percent that stays safe when single actuals are near zero.
TS = running sum of errors (RSFE) divided by running MAD. It grows when the forecast is biased in one direction.
About |TS| > 4, after a minimum number of periods. Some teams use 3 to 6.

front: Why compare live error with a naive baseline?
back: Hard days raise the error of every model. The ratio shows if your model got worse.

front: Why can the same MAD hide a problem?
back: MAD ignores direction. Errors that are always positive (bias) look the same as alternating errors. TS shows the difference.
